arxiv-2101-12009.title: A Peculiar ICME Event in August 2018 Observed with the Global Muon Detector Network
arxiv-2101-12009.description: Abstract We demonstrate that global observations of high-energy cosmic rays contribute to understanding unique characteristics of a large-scale magnetic flux rope causing a magnetic storm in August 2018. Following a weak interplanetary shock on 25 August 2018, a magnetic flux rope caused an unexpectedly large geomagnetic storm.

arxiv-2203-01448.title: Counting Points on Igusa Varieties of Hodge Type
arxiv-2203-01448.creator: Sander Mack-Crane
arxiv-2203-01448.description: Abstract Igusa varieties are algebraic varieties that arise in the study of special fibers of Shimura varieties, and have demonstrated many applications in the Langlands program via a Langlands–Kottwitz style point-counting formula due to Shin [ Shi09 ] in the case of PEL type.

arxiv-2305-03438.title: Dynamical self-trapping of two-dimensional binary solitons in cross-combined linear and nonlinear optical lattices
arxiv-2305-03438.creator: K.K. Ismailov 1,3 , G.A. Sekh 2 , and Mario Salerno 3
arxiv-2305-03438.description: Abstract Dynamical and self-trapping properties of two-dimensional (2D) binary mixtures of Bose-Einstein condensates (BECs) in cross-combined lattices consisting of a one-dimensional (1D) linear optical lattice (LOL) in the x-direction for the first component and a 1D non linear optical lattice (NOL) in the y y -direction for the second component, are analytically and numerically investigated.

arxiv-2312-09498.title: Neural Gaussian Similarity Modeling for Differential Graph Structure Learning
arxiv-2312-09498.creator: Xiaolong Fan, Maoguo Gong, Yue Wu, Zedong Tang, Jieyi Liu
arxiv-2312-09498.description: Abstract Graph Structure Learning (GSL) has demonstrated considerable potential in the analysis of graph-unknown non-Euclidean data across a wide range of domains. However, constructing an end-to-end graph structure learning model poses a challenge due to the impediment of gradient flow caused by the nearest neighbor sampling strategy.

arxiv-2602-04899.title: Phantom Transfer: Data-level Defences are Insufficient Against Data Poisoning
arxiv-2602-04899.creator: Andrew Draganov, Tolga H. Dur, Anandmayi Bhongade, Mary Phuong
arxiv-2602-04899.description: Abstract We present a data poisoning attack—Phantom Transfer—with the property that, even if you know precisely how the poison was placed into an otherwise benign dataset, you cannot filter it out. We achieve this by modifying subliminal learning to work in real-world contexts and demonstrate that the attack works across models, including GPT-4.1.

pmc-10673705.title: Multifocal Ectopic Recurrence of a C2 Chordoma
pmc-10673705.creator: Maikerly Reyes, Allison Kayne, Sarah Collopy, Giyarpuram Prashant, Patrick Kelly, James J. Evans
pmc-10673705.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Background Chordomas are histologically benign but locally aggressive tumors with a high propensity to recur. Our case highlights the importance of long-term vigilance in patients who have undergone chordoma resection. Case Report We report the case of a 47-year-old man with a cervical chordoma who developed multiple musculoskeletal ectopic recurrences in the left supraclavicular region, the proximal right bicep, and the left submandibular region without recurrence in the primary tumor site.

pmc-11290725.title: Evaluation of software technical quality for collecting data from patients under palliative care
pmc-11290725.creator: Jéssica de Fátima Gomes Pereira, Letícia Pontes, Mitzy Tannia Reichembach Danski, Solena Ziemer Kusma Fidalski, Juliana de Oliveira dos Santos, Maria Gorete de Brito Cunha, Mairla Cristina Silva Mota, Edmilson Bezerra Cruz, Jéssica de Fátima Gomes Pereira, Letícia Pontes, Mitzy Tannia Reichembach Da
pmc-11290725.description: Objectives:to evaluate software technical quality for collecting data from patients under palliative care.Methods:this is methodological technology evaluation research, according to the technical standard International Organization for Standardization/International Electrotechnical Commission 25040-2011, developed from August 2021 to August 2023. Eight nurses and eight information technology professionals participated as judges, who evaluated six quality characteristics and 23 subcharacteristics.

pmc-11458662.title: The involvement of multiple ABC transporters in daunorubicin efflux in Streptomyces coeruleorubidus
pmc-11458662.creator: Jianxin Dong, Jiali Ning, Yu Tian, Han Li, Hua Chen, Wenjun Guan
pmc-11458662.description: Streptomyces genus produces a large number of antibiotics, which are always synthesized by specific biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs). To resist autotoxicity, transporters encoded by genes located within BGC occasionally pump antibiotic along with transporter encoded by gene located outside BGC. Daunorubicin is an anthracycline antibiotic biosynthesized by Streptomyces species, playing a crucial role in the treatment of leukaemia.

pmc-11484982.title: The impact of explaining vegetarian meal requests on the affective responses and perceptions of meat eaters
pmc-11484982.creator: Kate Laffan, Emma Howard
pmc-11484982.description: Social situations can present challenges for those looking to reduce or avoid eating meat. In an experimental vignette study with a large representative sample of 1,117 UK-based meat eaters, we explore affective responses to requests for vegetarian meals and perceptions of those making the request across four social situations: a BBQ, a pub, a restaurant dinner, and a dinner party.

pmc-12452546.title: The structure and function of FBXW5 in human diseases
pmc-12452546.creator: Yuyang Han, Tao Yu, Zhaowu Ma
pmc-12452546.description: FBXW5, a member of the F-box protein family, plays a pivotal role in various cellular processes through its involvement in ubiquitin-mediated proteolysis as a component of the SCF complex. Recent studies have highlighted the potential of targeting FBXW5 for therapeutic interventions, making it a promising candidate for drug development.

pmc-12464680.title: El Niño-Southern Oscillation and shifting malaria risks in the Amazon
pmc-12464680.creator: Gabriel Zorello Laporta
pmc-12464680.description: llapse of the Classic Maya civilization,1 yet it also serves as a cautionary illustration of the vulnerabilities Amazonia faces under today's climatic and social pressures.2 In this context, a recent study by Arisco and colleagues in The Lancet Regional Health—Americas highlights the complex interplay between climate variability, including El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO) events, and malaria transmission in local Amazonian communities.

pmc-12694810.title: Molecular signatures of varicosity: Diagnostic insights from ten biomarkers
pmc-12694810.creator: Apurba Ganguly, Sudip Kumar Banerjee, Vidya Sagar Gubby Venkatesh, Dinesh Kumar Singal, Anondeep Ganguly
pmc-12694810.description: Background:Varicose veins are a chronic vascular disorder influenced by factors such as inflammation, fibrosis, endothelial dysfunction, and vascular cell activation. This study evaluates the association between ten molecular biomarkers and these risk factors in patients with lower extremity varicosity to enhance understanding of the condition's pathophysiology and highlight potential diagnostic biomarkers.

pmc-12731777.title: Prediction of Lymphovascular Invasion in Early–Stage Lung Adenocarcinoma Using Artificial Intelligence–Based Radiomics
pmc-12731777.creator: Yoshihisa Shimada, Kazuharu Harada, Yujin Kudo, Jinho Park, Jun Matsubayashi, Masataka Taguri, Norihiko Ikeda, Dania Cioni
pmc-12731777.description: Simple SummaryThe study developed an artificial intelligence (AI)–based radiomics model using a modified U–Net for lung nodule segmentation and a VGG–16–based convolutional network to predict lymphovascular invasion (LVI) in stage 0–I lung adenocarcinoma. Computed tomography (CT) data from 1265 patients were analyzed, and a risk score derived from 35 imaging features was validated in an independent cohort.

pmc-13340251.title: ProMeta: a meta-learning framework for robust disease diagnosis and prediction from plasma proteomics
pmc-13340251.creator: Han Li, Haoteng Gu, Lei Hu, Zimo Zhang, Yongji Lv, Peng Gao, Johnathan Cooper-Knock, Yaosen Min, Jianyang Zeng, Sai Zhang
pmc-13340251.description: MotivationThe plasma proteome offers a dynamic window of human health, capturing the real-time intersections between genetics and physiology. However, the application of deep learning to proteomics is currently hindered by a reliance on large-scale labeled datasets, rendering standard models ineffective for rare or novel diseases where patient samples are inherently scarce.

pmc-13653999.title: Wesselsbron virus at the livestock–human interface: A practical guide to disease recognition and diagnosis
pmc-13653999.creator: Kelly Garina Mugisha, Obdulio García-Nicolás, Moses M. Njire, Cecilia R. Waruhiu, Charaf Benarafa, Eric M. Fèvre
pmc-13653999.description: Wesselsbron virus (WSLV) is a mosquito-borne Orthoflavivirus of the yellow fever virus (YFV) serocomplex, widely distributed across sub-Saharan Africa. It is neglected, and its true impact is likely underestimated. WSLV causes abortion, congenital malformations, and neonatal mortality in sheep, the primary recognized vertebrate host, but infections have also been documented in goats, cattle, camels, wildlife, and humans.
